230: func (h *handler) handleOperationEvents(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, id string) {
231: 	lastID, err := parseEventID(r.Header.Get("Last-Event-ID"))
232: 	if err != nil {
233: 		h.writeOperationError(w, r, err)
234: 		return
235: 	}
236: 	replay, events, unsubscribe, err := h.hub.subscribe(sessionID(r.Context()), id, lastID)
237: 	if err != nil {
238: 		if h.followDurableOperationEvents(w, r, id, lastID) {
239: 			return
240: 		}
241: 		if legacyOperationID(id) {
242: 			h.writeError(w, r, http.StatusGone, "legacy_operation_not_retained", "This pre-durable operation is no longer retained. Refresh the owning product or inspect canonical workspace runs.")
243: 			return
244: 		}
245: 		h.writeOperationError(w, r, err)
246: 		return
247: 	}
248: 	defer unsubscribe()
249: 	flusher, ok := w.(http.Flusher)
250: 	if !ok {
251: 		h.writeOperationError(w, r, errors.New("streaming unavailable"))
252: 		return
253: 	}
254: 	_ = http.NewResponseController(w).SetWriteDeadline(h.now().Add(MaxStreamLifetime + SSEHeartbeat))
255: 	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream; charset=utf-8")
256: 	w.Header().Set("Connection", "keep-alive")
257: 	w.Header().Set("X-Accel-Buffering", "no")
258: 	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
259: 	for _, event := range replay {
260: 		if err := writeSSEEvent(w, event); err != nil {
261: 			return
262: 		}
263: 	}
264: 	flusher.Flush()
265: 	heartbeat := time.NewTicker(SSEHeartbeat)
266: 	defer heartbeat.Stop()
267: 	lifetime := time.NewTimer(MaxStreamLifetime)
268: 	defer lifetime.Stop()
269: 	for {
270: 		select {
271: 		case event, open := <-events:
272: 			if !open {
273: 				flusher.Flush()
274: 				return
275: 			}
276: 			if err := writeSSEEvent(w, event); err != nil {
277: 				return
278: 			}
279: 			flusher.Flush()
280: 		case <-heartbeat.C:
281: 			if _, err := io.WriteString(w, ": heartbeat\n\n"); err != nil {
282: 				return
283: 			}
284: 			flusher.Flush()
285: 		case <-lifetime.C:
286: 			return
287: 		case <-r.Context().Done():
288: 			return
289: 		}
290: 	}
291: }

444: // followDurableOperationEvents is the compatibility projection for a run that
445: // was accepted by this or another local server but is absent from this
446: // process's transient operation hub.
447: func (h *handler) followDurableOperationEvents(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, id string, after uint64) bool {
448: 	if h.runs == nil {
449: 		return false
450: 	}
451: 	snapshot, err := h.runs.Run(r.Context(), app.RunID(id))
452: 	if err != nil || string(snapshot.RunID) != id || snapshot.Target.Kind != "operation" {
453: 		return false
454: 	}
455: 	if after > snapshot.LastSequence {
456: 		h.writeError(w, r, http.StatusConflict, "cursor_ahead", "The event cursor is ahead of the durable operation.")
457: 		return true
458: 	}
459: 	if after+1 < snapshot.OldestRetainedSequence {
460: 		h.writeError(w, r, http.StatusConflict, "replay_gap", "The requested operation history is no longer retained; refresh its canonical run.")
461: 		return true
462: 	}
463: 	flusher, ok := w.(http.Flusher)
464: 	if !ok {
465: 		h.writeOperationError(w, r, errors.New("streaming unavailable"))
466: 		return true
467: 	}
468: 	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream; charset=utf-8")
469: 	w.Header().Set("Connection", "keep-alive")
470: 	w.Header().Set("X-Accel-Buffering", "no")
471: 	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
472: 	flusher.Flush()
473: 	heartbeat := time.NewTicker(SSEHeartbeat)
474: 	defer heartbeat.Stop()
475: 	lifetime := time.NewTimer(MaxStreamLifetime)
476: 	defer lifetime.Stop()
477: 	poll := time.NewTimer(0)
478: 	defer poll.Stop()
479: 	for {
480: 		select {
481: 		case <-poll.C:
482: 			events, eventErr := h.runs.RunEvents(r.Context(), snapshot.RunID, after, 512)
483: 			if eventErr != nil {
484: 				return true
485: 			}
486: 			for _, event := range events {
487: 				projected := durableOperationEvent(event)
488: 				if err := writeSSEEvent(w, projected); err != nil {
489: 					return true
490: 				}
491: 				after = event.Sequence
492: 			}
493: 			flusher.Flush()
494: 			snapshot, eventErr = h.runs.Run(r.Context(), snapshot.RunID)
495: 			if eventErr != nil || snapshot.Lifecycle.IsTerminal() && after >= snapshot.LastSequence {
496: 				return true
497: 			}
498: 			wait := time.Second
499: 			if len(events) == 512 || after < snapshot.LastSequence {
500: 				wait = 250 * time.Millisecond
501: 			}
502: 			poll.Reset(wait)
503: 		case <-heartbeat.C:
504: 			if _, err := io.WriteString(w, ": heartbeat\n\n"); err != nil {
505: 				return true
506: 			}
507: 			flusher.Flush()
508: 		case <-lifetime.C:
509: 			return true
510: 		case <-r.Context().Done():
511: 			return true
512: 		}
513: 	}
514: }

516: func durableOperationEvent(event app.RunEvent) operationEvent {
517: 	name := "progress"
518: 	switch string(event.Type) {
519: 	case "accepted", "claimed", "lifecycle":
520: 		name = "snapshot"
521: 	case "warning", "finding", "artifact", "terminal":
522: 		name = string(event.Type)
523: 	case "cancellation":
524: 		name = "cancel_requested"
525: 	case "recovery", "omission":
526: 		name = "recovery_required"
527: 	}
528: 	payload := map[string]any{"stage": event.Stage, "task": event.Task, "payload": event.Payload, "omission": event.Omission}
529: 	body, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
530: 		"operation_id": string(event.RunID), "time": event.CommittedAt.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
531: 		"sequence": event.Sequence, "payload": payload,
532: 	})
533: 	return operationEvent{ID: event.Sequence, Name: name, Data: body}
534: }

536: func operationSpecFromForm(r *http.Request) operationSpecRequest {
537: 	parallelism, _ := strconv.Atoi(r.FormValue("parallelism"))
538: 	sprintRef := r.FormValue("sprint")
539: 	if sprintRef == "" {
540: 		sprintRef = newSprintRef(r.FormValue("sprint_number"), r.FormValue("sprint_name"))
541: 	}

230: func (h *handler) handleOperationEvents(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, id string) {
231: 	lastID, err := parseEventID(r.Header.Get("Last-Event-ID"))
232: 	if err != nil {
233: 		h.writeOperationError(w, r, err)
234: 		return
235: 	}
236: 	replay, events, unsubscribe, err := h.hub.subscribe(sessionID(r.Context()), id, lastID)
237: 	if err != nil {
238: 		if h.followDurableOperationEvents(w, r, id, lastID) {
239: 			return
240: 		}
241: 		if legacyOperationID(id) {
242: 			h.writeError(w, r, http.StatusGone, "legacy_operation_not_retained", "This pre-durable operation is no longer retained. Refresh the owning product or inspect canonical workspace runs.")
243: 			return
244: 		}
245: 		h.writeOperationError(w, r, err)
246: 		return
247: 	}
248: 	defer unsubscribe()
249: 	flusher, ok := w.(http.Flusher)
250: 	if !ok {
251: 		h.writeOperationError(w, r, errors.New("streaming unavailable"))
252: 		return
253: 	}
254: 	_ = http.NewResponseController(w).SetWriteDeadline(h.now().Add(MaxStreamLifetime + SSEHeartbeat))
255: 	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream; charset=utf-8")
256: 	w.Header().Set("Connection", "keep-alive")
257: 	w.Header().Set("X-Accel-Buffering", "no")
258: 	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
259: 	for _, event := range replay {
260: 		if err := writeSSEEvent(w, event); err != nil {
261: 			return
262: 		}
263: 	}
264: 	flusher.Flush()
265: 	heartbeat := time.NewTicker(SSEHeartbeat)
266: 	defer heartbeat.Stop()
267: 	lifetime := time.NewTimer(MaxStreamLifetime)
268: 	defer lifetime.Stop()
269: 	for {
270: 		select {
271: 		case event, open := <-events:
272: 			if !open {
273: 				flusher.Flush()
274: 				return
275: 			}
276: 			if err := writeSSEEvent(w, event); err != nil {
277: 				return
278: 			}
279: 			flusher.Flush()
280: 		case <-heartbeat.C:
281: 			if _, err := io.WriteString(w, ": heartbeat\n\n"); err != nil {
282: 				return
283: 			}
284: 			flusher.Flush()
285: 		case <-lifetime.C:
286: 			return
287: 		case <-r.Context().Done():
288: 			return
289: 		}
290: 	}
291: }

444: // followDurableOperationEvents is the compatibility projection for a run that
445: // was accepted by this or another local server but is absent from this
446: // process's transient operation hub.
447: func (h *handler) followDurableOperationEvents(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, id string, after uint64) bool {
448: 	if h.runs == nil {
449: 		return false
450: 	}
451: 	snapshot, err := h.runs.Run(r.Context(), app.RunID(id))
452: 	if err != nil || string(snapshot.RunID) != id || snapshot.Target.Kind != "operation" {
453: 		return false
454: 	}
455: 	if after > snapshot.LastSequence {
456: 		h.writeError(w, r, http.StatusConflict, "cursor_ahead", "The event cursor is ahead of the durable operation.")
457: 		return true
458: 	}
459: 	if after+1 < snapshot.OldestRetainedSequence {
460: 		h.writeError(w, r, http.StatusConflict, "replay_gap", "The requested operation history is no longer retained; refresh its canonical run.")
461: 		return true
462: 	}
463: 	flusher, ok := w.(http.Flusher)
464: 	if !ok {
465: 		h.writeOperationError(w, r, errors.New("streaming unavailable"))
466: 		return true
467: 	}
468: 	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream; charset=utf-8")
469: 	w.Header().Set("Connection", "keep-alive")
470: 	w.Header().Set("X-Accel-Buffering", "no")
471: 	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
472: 	flusher.Flush()
473: 	heartbeat := time.NewTicker(SSEHeartbeat)
474: 	defer heartbeat.Stop()
475: 	lifetime := time.NewTimer(MaxStreamLifetime)
476: 	defer lifetime.Stop()
477: 	poll := time.NewTimer(0)
478: 	defer poll.Stop()
479: 	for {
480: 		select {
481: 		case <-poll.C:
482: 			events, eventErr := h.runs.RunEvents(r.Context(), snapshot.RunID, after, 512)
483: 			if eventErr != nil {
484: 				return true
485: 			}
486: 			for _, event := range events {
487: 				projected := durableOperationEvent(event)
488: 				if err := writeSSEEvent(w, projected); err != nil {
489: 					return true
490: 				}
491: 				after = event.Sequence
492: 			}
493: 			flusher.Flush()
494: 			snapshot, eventErr = h.runs.Run(r.Context(), snapshot.RunID)
495: 			if eventErr != nil || snapshot.Lifecycle.IsTerminal() && after >= snapshot.LastSequence {
496: 				return true
497: 			}
498: 			wait := time.Second
499: 			if len(events) == 512 || after < snapshot.LastSequence {
500: 				wait = 250 * time.Millisecond
501: 			}
502: 			poll.Reset(wait)
503: 		case <-heartbeat.C:
504: 			if _, err := io.WriteString(w, ": heartbeat\n\n"); err != nil {
505: 				return true
506: 			}
507: 			flusher.Flush()
508: 		case <-lifetime.C:
509: 			return true
510: 		case <-r.Context().Done():
511: 			return true
512: 		}
513: 	}
514: }

516: func durableOperationEvent(event app.RunEvent) operationEvent {
517: 	name := "progress"
518: 	switch string(event.Type) {
519: 	case "accepted", "claimed", "lifecycle":
520: 		name = "snapshot"
521: 	case "warning", "finding", "artifact", "terminal":
522: 		name = string(event.Type)
523: 	case "cancellation":
524: 		name = "cancel_requested"
525: 	case "recovery", "omission":
526: 		name = "recovery_required"
527: 	}
528: 	payload := map[string]any{"stage": event.Stage, "task": event.Task, "payload": event.Payload, "omission": event.Omission}
529: 	body, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
530: 		"operation_id": string(event.RunID), "time": event.CommittedAt.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
531: 		"sequence": event.Sequence, "payload": payload,
532: 	})
533: 	return operationEvent{ID: event.Sequence, Name: name, Data: body}
534: }

556: func newSprintRef(number, name string) string {
557: 	number = strings.TrimSpace(number)
558: 	name = strings.TrimSpace(name)
559: 	if number == "" || name == "" {
560: 		return ""
561: 	}
562: 	for _, r := range number {
563: 		if r < '0' || r > '9' {
564: 			return number + "-" + name
565: 		}
566: 	}
567: 	var slug strings.Builder
568: 	separator := false
569: 	for _, r := range strings.ToLower(name) {
570: 		switch {
571: 		case r >= 'a' && r <= 'z', r >= '0' && r <= '9':
572: 			if separator && slug.Len() > 0 {
573: 				slug.WriteByte('-')
574: 			}
575: 			slug.WriteRune(r)
576: 			separator = false
577: 		case r == ' ' || r == '-' || r == '_':
578: 			separator = true
579: 		default:
580: 			return number + "-" + name
581: 		}
582: 	}
583: 	if slug.Len() == 0 {
584: 		return ""
585: 	}
586: 	return number + "-" + slug.String()
587: }

594: func decodeStrictJSON(r *http.Request, target any) error {
595: 	contentType := r.Header.Get("Content-Type")
596: 	if !strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(contentType), "application/json") {
597: 		return fmt.Errorf("Content-Type must be application/json")
598: 	}
599: 	decoder := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
600: 	decoder.DisallowUnknownFields()
601: 	if err := decoder.Decode(target); err != nil {
602: 		return fmt.Errorf("invalid JSON request: %w", err)
603: 	}
604: 	var extra any
605: 	if err := decoder.Decode(&extra); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
606: 		return fmt.Errorf("request must contain one JSON value")
607: 	}
608: 	return nil
609: }

611: func mapOperationRequest(spec operationSpecRequest) (app.OperationRequest, error) {
612: 	if !validOptionalIdentifier(spec.Scope.Project) || !validOptionalIdentifier(spec.Scope.Sprint) || !validOptionalIdentifier(spec.Scope.Study) {
613: 		return app.OperationRequest{}, fmt.Errorf("operation scope contains an invalid identifier")
614: 	}
615: 	options := spec.Options
616: 	req := app.OperationRequest{
617: 		Project: spec.Scope.Project, Sprint: spec.Scope.Sprint, Study: spec.Scope.Study,
618: 		Stage: firstString(options.ToStage, options.Stage), Task: options.Task, Model: options.Model,
619: 		Level: options.Level, Suite: options.Suite, Test: options.Test, Timeout: options.Timeout,
620: 		ForceReview: options.ForceReview, RestartReview: options.RestartReview, OverrideRationale: options.OverrideRationale,
621: 		ReviewFocus: options.ReviewFocus, Sources: options.Sources, Dimensions: options.Dimensions, Parallelism: options.Parallelism,
622: 	}
623: 	kind := strings.ReplaceAll(strings.TrimSpace(spec.Kind), "_", "-")
624: 	switch kind {
625: 	case "validation", "validate":
626: 		req.Kind = app.OperationValidate
627: 	case "sprint-status":
628: 		req.Kind = app.OperationSprintStatus
629: 	case "prompt-preview", "sprint-prompt":
630: 		req.Kind = app.OperationPrompt
631: 	case "dry-run", "sprint-flow-dry-run":

reasoning_details.text:
**Study-cancel SIGINT analysis:**

`CancelRunLoop`:
1. Reads lock file `studies/<study>/.ultraplan/run-loop.lock` (JSON with PID).
2. Checks `processAlive(info.PID)` — alive via kill(pid,0).
3. Checks `info.Study != study.Name` mismatch.
4. Refuses if PID == own process.
5. `syscall.Kill(info.PID, SIGINT)`.

Trust transition: the PID comes from a file inside the workspace studies directory. Who can write that file? The ultraplan process itself when starting run loops. But the workspace is user-editable data (markdown files etc.) — in this product, workspaces are governed artifacts possibly edited by collaborators or synced. If an attacker (or a malicious/corrupt workspace sync) can write `run-loop.lock` with an arbitrary live PID, then any door that runs OperationStudyCancel (TUI keypress, CLI command, web kind=study-cancel) will send SIGINT to an arbitrary local process owned by the same UID.

Is there validation? Lock JSON unmarshal; only checks Study name match and liveness. No check that the PID is actually an ultraplan process (e.g., comparing Command, /proc/PID/cmdline). A crafted lock with `{"pid": 1234, "study": "target-study", "path": ""}` → SIGINT to PID 1234 if alive and same-uid-permission.

Counter-evidence to consider:
- Attacker model: who can write into the workspace? The tool's threat model treats workspace files as governed inputs — fingerprinting rejects symlinks, displaySafe redacts... The product explicitly defends against hostile workspace content in other places (symlink rejection in fingerprints/previews, redaction of file-derived text). So "workspace content is partially trusted" is the operating assumption elsewhere. A lock-file PID → signal primitive is a genuine trust transition from workspace data to process control.
- Mitigation present: `info.Study != study.Name` check requires attacker to know target study name (trivial), and PID liveness. No cmdline verification.
- Consequence: SIGINT is relatively benign (graceful interrupt) but to arbitrary same-user processes — e.g., interrupting another long-running job, or an editor? SIGINT default action terminates most processes. It's a limited arbitrary-process-kill primitive (same UID). Severity: medium-low given local single-operator context; but it IS a real misuse path via attacker-controlled input (workspace file) crossing a trust boundary (file content → syscall).

Also PID reuse race: legitimate stale lock with dead PID whose number got reused by unrelated process → RunLoopActive says active → CancelRunLoop SIGINTs unrelated new process. That's the classic PID-reuse hazard; the liveness check makes stale-lock reuse *more* likely to hit wrong process rather than less. Note AcquireRunLoopLock handles stale locks by removing them when dead — but between death and reuse there's a window; after reuse, acquire sees alive PID and refuses (safe); cancel however signals it (unsafe). Hmm wait: acquire refuses because processAlive(existing.PID) true → error "held by pid" even though it's now a different process — that's a false-positive lock conflict (reliability). And cancel sends SIGINT to the reused PID. Both stem from trusting the recorded PID without identity verification.

But hold on — is this surface (`shared-usecase-vocabulary`) the right place for this finding? The entrypoint is OperationStudyCancel in sharedOperationRunner (operations vocabulary), reached through all three doors. Yes — cross-interface operation vocabulary includes StudyCancel semantics. In scope.

Let me also verify: does the web door allow study-cancel? mapOperationRequest has case "study-cancel". Yes! So a browser click can trigger SIGINT to the lock PID. And TUI ActionCancel on study view. And CLI study cancel command presumably calls CancelRunLoop directly too.

Verification/regression test: craft lock file with PID of a dummy process, invoke operation study-cancel, observe foreign process received SIGINT. Fix: record process identity (e.g., /proc/PID/cmdline prefix + start time from /proc/PID/stat field 22) in lock; validate before signaling.

Now **TUI digest**: basis = CanonicalRequest + "\x00" + InputFingerprint — computed ONLY when m.model.Confirmation != nil. For operations without confirmation flow? All TUI ops go through confirmationCmd first (Confirmation set). StudyCancel via beginOperation at line 139: `m.beginOperation(app.OperationRequest{Kind: app.OperationStudyCancel, Study: study})` — called WITHOUT setting m.model.Confirmation! So manager type-assert ok but Confirmation==nil → digest branch skipped → AcceptOperation NOT called at all → study-cancel runs WITHOUT durable acceptance! 1. **`beginOperation` uses `m.model.Confirmation` regardless of which `req` is passed.** The study-cancel ladder at line 139 calls `m.beginOperation(app.OperationRequest{Kind: OperationStudyCancel, Study: study})`. If `m.model.Confirmation != nil` at that moment (a pending confirmation for a DIFFERENT operation X), then:
   - digest computed over X's canonical request+fingerprint,
   - `AcceptOperation(ctx, *Confirmation, digest)` → creates durable run for X (Target.Operation = X.Kind, alias = digest(X)),
   - `acceptedRunID = runID of X`,
   - then `operationCmd(opctx, req=study-cancel, acceptedRunID(X), stream)` runs the STUDY CANCEL under run X's identity; events recorded onto X's run; FinishOperation(X, complete) marks X succeeded.
   - Result: durable row claims operation X ran and succeeded, while the actual side effect was cancelling study S. And X can never be started again via TUI (alias hit → "matching durable operation already exists" with lifecycle "succeeded").

Reachability: need Confirmation non-nil while pressing 'c' on a study view with !Running. When is Confirmation set? confirmationCmd returns ConfirmationMsg → model.Update handles it (in model package — tui model.go?). Need to check: does ConfirmationMsg handler clear on navigation (ActionBack)? Let me read internal/tui/model.go (or wherever Model.Update handles ConfirmationMsg) to see when Confirmation is cleared.

Also note ActionConfirm path (line 102): requires Confirmation != nil && !Running. If user prepares op X (Confirmation set), then instead of Enter presses 'c'... conditions at line 107: Running false → skip 108/118; route not RouteRun presumably; study := RunViewStudy or selected item ViewRun... If they're on a study view having prepared something earlier — plausible navigation flow.

2. **TUI event recording drops events silently**: in operationCmd emit closure — RecordOperationEvent error → `return` (event NOT forwarded to stream either!). So on persistence error, TUI shows nothing (no warning), though manager cancels ctx internally so operation will fail soon. Also `committed == false` (coalesced) → dropped from stream too. OK by design.

3. **TUI FinishOperation failure joined into e** — displayed. Fine.

4. **dashboardAndRuns**: Runs query without TargetKind filter — TUI lists ALL runs incl. future non-operation kinds; fine.

5. **TUI cancel ladder line 110/124: CancelRun(...,"user_requested")** — no Target.Kind recheck; cancels any run id shown in list (all kinds). Parity divergence noted in pack.

Now let me find where ConfirmationMsg is handled and whether navigation clears Confirmation.

reasoning_details.text:
Key finding on ConfirmationMsg handling (line 213-222):

```go
case ConfirmationMsg:
	m.Loading = false
	if v.Route != m.currentRoute() {
		return m   // stale confirmation DROPPED, m.Confirmation unchanged!
	}
	...
	m.Confirmation = &v.Result
```

If the route changed between request and response, the Confirmation is discarded (not stored). Good. But `m.Confirmation` is NOT cleared on navigation generally! ActionBack clears it only in a specific else-if chain position: after ParallelForm and RunViewStudy checks — `else if m.Confirmation != nil { m.Confirmation = nil }`. But other navigations do NOT clear Confirmation:
- ActionFocusNext (tab switch) — no clear.
- setTab via KeyMsg 'projects'/'studies' etc. — need to see; likely no clear.
- Selecting another item (ActionOpen on different item) → confirmationCmd for new item → ConfirmationMsg with Route check → if same route, REPLACES m.Confirmation. If different route, dropped.

Scenario for stale-Confirmation + study-cancel mismatch:
1. User on sprint view prepares op X (e.g., execute-start) → Confirmation(X) set, confirm screen shown.
2. Instead of Enter, user switches tab to studies (ActionFocusNext) or navigates... Does any navigation clear? ActionBack would clear (else-if), but tab switch does not. So Confirmation(X) persists while viewing studies tab.
3. On study view, press 'c' (ActionCancel): Running false; route not RouteRun; RunViewStudy empty unless opened run view; selectedItem().ViewRun → study name S non-empty → beginOperation(study-cancel S) with m.model.Confirmation = X still set!
4. beginOperation: manager ok && Confirmation != nil → digest over X's canonical → AcceptOperation(ctx, X's confirmation, digest(X)) → durable run created for X (kind execute-start!), claimed, lifecycle running event.
5. operationCmd runs req = study-cancel → sends SIGINT to study run-loop PID.
6. FinishOperation(runX, complete) → row says execute-start succeeded.
7. Later pressing Enter/confirming X again: digest matches alias → Existing=true lifecycle "succeeded" → "matching durable operation already exists" — operator blocked from ever starting X via TUI until retention/compaction removes the alias.

Wait — step 7: Existing path shows message but doesn't run. To actually run X they'd have to use web or CLI. The alias persists in run-control DB indefinitely (until compaction?). This is a genuine correctness defect with concrete bad outcome, triggered by ordinary TUI navigation (no attacker needed).

But hold on — verify that ActionFocusNext/tab switching really doesn't clear Confirmation, and check whether views show the confirm screen only on the route where prepared. Also check whether pressing 'c' on studies tab requires selectedItem with ViewRun. Let me look at model.go more (setTab, selectedItem, ViewRun population) and keys.go for action mapping ('c' = cancel).

Also double-check line 139 reachability conditions again:
```go
case ActionCancel:
	if m.model.Running && ... // false
	if m.model.Running && m.cancel != nil // false
	if route := currentRoute(); route.Kind == RouteRun && route.RunID != "" // if user is on a run detail view, cancels THAT run instead
	study := m.model.RunViewStudy
	if study == "" { if item, ok := selectedItem(); ok { study = item.ViewRun } }
	if study != "" && !Running { return m.beginOperation({Kind: OperationStudyCancel, Study: study}) }
```
So yes: on studies tab with a selected study item having ViewRun set, pressing 'c' begins study-cancel. If Confirmation(X) pending → mislabeled acceptance.

Also even WITHOUT stale confirmation: beginOperation(study-cancel) with Confirmation nil → NO durable acceptance at all → study-cancel runs without any durable row (divergence vs web door which creates one). Two distinct findings:

**Finding A**: TUI study-cancel performs AcceptOperation with whatever stale Confirmation happens to be pending, recording the WRONG operation durably (Target.Operation/digest of unrelated op) while executing study-cancel — permanent alias squatting blocks future TUI starts of that op.

**Finding B**: TUI study-cancel with no pending Confirmation bypasses durable acceptance entirely — no run-control row, no audit trail, diverging from web door semantics for the same logical action.

Both stem from beginOperation conflating "pending Confirmation" with "request being begun". Let me verify keys.go mapping of 'c' and check setTab/selectedItem ViewRun. Also verify OperationMsg handler clears Confirmation (line 234) — after ANY operation completes, Confirmation=nil. But during the window (prepared, not yet started), the stale path exists.

Also check: does the confirm screen render modally such that other keys are ignored? In teaModel.Update, KeyMsg handled before model.Update — the outer handler intercepts ActionCancel regardless of Confirmation display state. The model.Update KeyMsg also processes... both run: teaModel.Update case tea.KeyMsg handles actions AND then calls m.model.Update(KeyMsg(...)) in default branches — but for ActionCancel it returns early (line 141 `return m, nil`). So yes outer handler wins.

package tui

type KeyAction string

const (
	ActionNone         KeyAction = "none"
	ActionQuit         KeyAction = "quit"
	ActionUp           KeyAction = "up"
	ActionDown         KeyAction = "down"
	ActionProjects     KeyAction = "projects"
	ActionStudies      KeyAction = "studies"
	ActionRuns         KeyAction = "runs"
	ActionRefresh      KeyAction = "refresh"
	ActionOpen         KeyAction = "open"
	ActionClosePreview KeyAction = "close-preview"
	ActionFocusNext    KeyAction = "focus-next"
	ActionBack         KeyAction = "back"
	ActionLeft         KeyAction = "left"
	ActionRight        KeyAction = "right"
	ActionConfirm      KeyAction = "confirm"
	ActionCancel       KeyAction = "cancel"
)

func KeyToAction(key string) KeyAction {
	switch key {
	case "q", "ctrl+c":
		return ActionQuit
	case "esc", "backspace":
		return ActionBack
	case "tab", "shift+tab":
		return ActionFocusNext
	case "left", "h":
		return ActionLeft
	case "right", "l":
		return ActionRight
	case "up", "k":
		return ActionUp
	case "down", "j":
		return ActionDown
	case "1", "p":
		return ActionProjects
	case "2", "u":
		return ActionStudies
	case "w":
		return ActionRuns
	case "r":
		return ActionRefresh
	case "c":
		return ActionCancel
	case "enter", "o":
		return ActionOpen
	default:
		return ActionNone
	}
}

func HelpText() string {
	return "q quit | tab switch Projects/Studies | w runs | arrows navigate | enter open/confirm | c request cancellation | esc back | r refresh"
}

Nothing blocks input while Loading=true. Later attempts to start X via TUI → Existing hit → permanently blocked ("matching durable operation already exists") until alias retention ends.

reasoning_details.text:
`Target.Validate`: bounds + rejects \x00 \r \n only. **ESC (0x1b) is NOT rejected** — and other control chars (0x01-0x08, 0x0b, 0x0c, 0x0e-0x1f, 0x7f) are NOT rejected either. Only NUL, CR, LF.

So: Target.Stage/Task from a web `options.stage`/`options.task`/`shard`, or TUI... web mapOperationRequest does NOT validate Stage charset. A malicious/curious local HTTP client can POST prepare with kind=sprint-stage, options.stage = "\x1b[31;1mINJECTED\x1b[0m" (no CR/LF/NUL — ESC is fine!). PrepareOperation → validateOperationScope ignores Stage → Confirmation OK → confirm/start → AcceptOperation persists Target.Stage with raw ESC sequences into runs.stage_id.

Then where do stage/task get RENDERED?
- Web run pages: run_handlers views — HTML-escaped by html/template ✓ safe.
- API JSON: escaped ✓.
- **TUI Runs tab**: label = run.Target.Kind + "/" + run.Target.Operation (model.go:565) — Operation not Stage. Operation comes from enum via all doors... EXCEPT: durableOperationDocument Kind=app.OperationKind(snapshot.Target.Operation) — Operation persisted from req.Kind which is always an enum value through all doors ✓. So Operation safe.
- Stage rendered in TUI run detail view? Let me check run_view rendering of events' Stage/Task fields: RunEvent.Stage/Task come from EventDraft sanitize → safeEventValue strips only NUL/CR/LF too! So event Stage/Task with ESC survive into TUI rendering. Do TUI views render event.Stage/Task raw? Check views.go/run_view for how events are displayed — bubbletea renders plain strings to terminal; ANSI in strings IS interpreted by the terminal unless stripped!

Where can attacker-controlled data enter event.Stage/Task? RecordOperationEvent: Stage: event.Stage — runner sets Stage from progress.Stage (sprint stages — fixed), Task from p.Task.ID / CoverageID / shard IDs — derived from workspace files (plan.md task IDs, QA shard IDs). Workspace files are governed inputs that ultraplan explicitly treats as potentially hostile (symlink rejection, displaySafe redaction of findings/messages). Task IDs from plan.md could contain ESC? Markdown parsing might preserve them. That's the study/sprint surface's problem though; through THIS surface, the direct injection vector is web options.stage/options.task/shard/model etc. — Model flows into... Target? No. Model goes into canonical JSON + runtime identity string ("requested model "+req.Model) → Confirmation.ModelSource → preparationDTO.Runtime.model → browser JSON ✓ escaped. Not terminal-rendered.

But Stage/Task DO land in runs row columns AND events (RecordOperationEvent Stage/Task) AND CLI `run follow` text output: `fmt.Fprintf(deps.stdout, "%d  %-14s %s%s\n", event.Sequence, event.Type, event.Stage, ...)` — RAW fmt.Fprintf to terminal! An attacker who can influence event.Stage/Task (via crafted plan.md task IDs reaching runner events, or via web door stage field → wait, does the web door's Stage reach EVENTS? RecordOperationEvent uses event.Stage which runners set from sprint internals, not from req.Stage... For flow ops: tuiSprintRuntimeProgress sets Stage: string(progress.Stage) — parsed PlanningStage (fixed values). ExecuteStart: no stage set except "execute" literals. QA: progress.Phase fixed-ish. Study: p.Event strings fixed.

Hmm so event.Stage sources are product-fixed enums mostly. The durable RUNS ROW target.stage though comes straight from req.Stage via all doors. Who renders target.stage? TUI Runs tab label doesn't include it. Run detail view (run_view.go)? Let me check what run view renders — maybe Target fields. And web run pages escape HTML. CLI `run show` renderRunSnapshot — prints snapshot incl. target fields RAW to terminal? renderRunSnapshot at run_commands.go:380-430ish — let me check if it Fprintf's Target.Stage/Task unescaped. If yes: cross-door ANSI injection — attacker lures local operator to open a malicious page (CSRF-protected though! mutations need session+CSRF+origin). Hmm — but prepare requires valid session + origin + CSRF. Attacker page can't forge those (SameSite=Strict cookie + CSRF token derived from session secret). Could a malicious LOCAL process call the API directly? It's loopback-only but any local process can hit 127.0.0.1:8080 — middleware requires session cookie + CSRF header for mutations; a local non-browser client can simply OBTAIN a session: GET / returns Set-Cookie signed session + X-CSRF-Token header in response! Then POST with cookie+header+Origin: http://127.0.0.1:8080. So ANY local process can drive the operation API fully (that's inherent to a local dashboard without auth — the security model is "same-user local processes are trusted", same UID threat). Given that, injecting ESC into stage_id is trivially possible for any local process — but such a process could equally write the workspace files directly or signal processes directly. Escalation value ≈ nil within same-UID threat model. The remaining exposure: a REMOTE party who controls plan.md content (collaborator pushing governed artifacts) → task IDs with ESC → rendered raw in operator's terminal via run follow/TUI. That crosses a trust boundary the codebase elsewhere defends (displaySafe exists precisely for this). But whether task IDs actually flow unredacted into terminal output depends on sprint/study surfaces' parsing, beyond this surface's evidence. I'll note the missing ESC rejection in Target.Validate/event sanitization as a low-severity hardening gap tied to concrete sinks (CLI run follow raw Fprintf; TUI label rendering) — worth one line, not a headline.

Actually wait, let me verify renderRunSnapshot quickly for raw target printing, since CLI run show/follow are this surface's observation doors.

part.text:
Review complete. All evidence gathered against frozen commit `5d54525` (`internal/app`, `internal/web`, `internal/tui` identical to HEAD). Repro tests preserved at `review/jobs/findings-shared-usecase-vocabulary/`.

# Findings — `shared-usecase-vocabulary` (security/misuse lens)

## F1 · HIGH severity, HIGH confidence — TUI accepts a stale unrelated confirmation durably while executing a different operation, falsifying run-control and permanently alias-squatting the real operation

- **Claim**: `beginOperation` binds durable acceptance to whatever `Confirmation` happens to be pending, not to the request it is asked to run (`internal/tui/app.go:232-255`: digest and `AcceptOperation(ctx, *m.model.Confirmation, …)` use `m.model.Confirmation`, while the executed request is the `req` parameter).
- **Trigger**: The only caller that passes a divergent `req` is the study-cancel ladder (`app.go:139`). `Model.setTab` and route navigation never clear `Confirmation` (`internal/tui/model.go:359-374`; only `ActionBack`/`OperationMsg`/same-route guards do, model.go:234, 265-266). Sequence: prepare any operation X (e.g., execute-start) → switch tabs/routes without `esc` → open a study whose summary has `RunActive` (first nav item carries `ViewRun`, model.go:542-543) → press `c`.
- **Execution path**: `ActionCancel` → `beginOperation({Kind: OperationStudyCancel})` → `AcceptOperation(X's confirmation, sha256(canonical_X‖fp_X))` creates a durable run with `Target.Operation=execute-start`, claims it, emits lifecycle-running → `RunOperation(study-cancel)` executes under that run id → `FinishOperation(complete)` proposes terminal `succeeded`.
- **Observable bad outcomes** (both proven by executed test against `5d54525`, output: `PROOF: durable accept recorded kind="execute-start" … while executed kind="study-cancel"`):
  1. Run-control permanently records that execute-start ran and succeeded when only a SIGINT was sent — violating the truthfulness contract ("Every runtime-backed … operation receives a durable run", user-guide.md:374-391; "compacted/tombstone records remain truthful").
  2. Retrying X via TUI recomputes the identical content digest (unchanged inputs) → alias conflict → `Existing=true` → "matching durable operation already exists" (`app.go:245-250`) — the operator cannot start X via TUI until the alias cascades away with run deletion (~37 days at default retention: FullHistory 7d + Tombstone 30d, runcontrol/model.go:423-424).
- **Counter-evidence searched**: web door unaffected (token-bound dedup); CLI has no study-cancel command; no TUI test covers `beginOperation`/`StudyCancel` (grep: zero hits) so nothing pins this as intended.
- **Regression test**: the preserved repro (`stale_confirmation_repro_test.go`) asserts accepted kind ≠ executed kind. Fix shape: derive acceptance from `req` (re-prepare or require `req == Confirmation.Request.Kind/scope`), else skip durable acceptance.

## F2 · MEDIUM severity, HIGH confidence — readOnly composition split makes TUI the only door whose dashboard passively rewrites governed files, clobbering concurrent writers and cross-door invalidating QA fingerprints

- **Claim**: serve forces `readOnly:true` twice (`serve_commands.go:59`, `web_usecases.go:429`) → `sprintService().WithoutStatusWrites()` (`usecases.go:130-132`) suppresses writes; TUI composes without it (`tui_commands.go:41-46`).
- **Path**: every Dashboard load, `r` refresh, and 1 Hz run-view tick (`app.go:222-226, 271-273`) → `SprintSummaries` → `Status` per sprint (`sprint_usecases.go:482`) → unconditional `SaveFlowState` (`sprint/service.go:291-295`), which always rewrites bytes (`UpdatedAt = time.Now()`, `sprint/state.go:247`). No cross-process lock exists (only atomic temp+rename, state.go:259-290).
- **Observable bad outcomes**:
  1. Last-writer-wins lost updates against concurrent CLI/web processes writing flow-state.json (e.g., a review/smoke publication landing between Status's load and save is silently reverted until the next writer).
  2. `flow-state.json` is a governed fingerprint input for all QA kinds (`operations.go:678-685`); an open TUI changes its bytes every second, so a QA prepare→confirm sequence done elsewhere fails with `stale_confirmation` despite zero semantic change — cross-door interference caused purely by an idle dashboard.
  3. Contract contradiction: top-level help says "Open a read-only terminal dashboard" (`app.go:268`) while `tuiHelp` discloses status rewrites (`tui_commands.go:90`).
- **Regression test**: compose TUI use cases, call Dashboard twice, assert flow-state.json mtime/content unchanged (fails today; passes if TUI adopts `readOnly:true` or Status gates on content diff).

## F3 · MEDIUM severity, MEDIUM confidence — study-cancel converts workspace-file content (lock JSON PID) into a signal via liveness-only validation

- **Claim**: `study.CancelRunLoop` (`internal/study/locks.go:141-159`) reads `studies/<s>/.ultraplan/run-loop.lock`, checks only `processAlive(pid)` (`kill 0`) and the recorded study name, then `syscall.Kill(pid, SIGINT)`. No process-identity verification, unlike the careful `ProcessIdentity{HostDigest, BootID, BirthToken}` regime run-control uses for leases (`runcontrol/model.go:193-210`).
- **Trust transition / misuse**: anyone who can write workspace files (workspace sync, collaborator artifacts, malicious tooling) can place `{"pid":N,"study":"<name>"}` and have any operator door — TUI `c`, web `kind=study-cancel` (`operation_runner.go:152-162`) — SIGINT arbitrary same-UID process N. Independently, legitimate PID reuse makes `RunLoopActive` report a dead owner as live: cancel signals the innocent new process, and acquire false-reports "held by pid N".
- **Consequence**: limited (SIGINT to same-UID processes) but a genuine file-content→syscall primitive crossing the codebase's own governed-input hostility assumptions (symlink rejection, `displaySafe` redaction exist precisely because workspace content is treated as untrusted).
- **Regression test**: write lock with PID of a spawned dummy process, invoke OperationStudyCancel through `RunOperation`, assert foreign process signaled (fails today); fix: record and verify `/proc` cmdline prefix + start tick like run-control identity.

## F4 · LOW-MEDIUM — replay semantics diverge: CLI `run follow` silently serves post-compaction partial history where web enforces `replay_gap`

`repository.Events` returns only the retained tail with no gap signal (`runcontrol/sqlite.go:819-821`). Web durable fallback rejects `after+1 < OldestRetainedSequence` with `replay_gap` and cursor-ahead conflicts (`operation_handlers.go:455-461`; REST equivalent in run_handlers.go), but `run follow` (`run_commands.go:161-195`) prints whatever remains and exits 0 — an operator auditing a compacted run believes they captured the full journal. Same logical observation, opposite failure visibility.

## F5 · LOW — operations cancel endpoint skips the `Target.Kind=="operation"` gate its sibling projections enforce

`handleOperationStatus`/`durableOperationStatus`/`followDurableOperationEvents` all require `Target.Kind=="operation"` (`operation_handlers.go:364, 416, 452`), but both cancel handlers fall back to `runs.CancelRun(id)` for **any** run id (`:206-213, 381-396`), cancelling non-operation runs and echoing their kind/reason/state. Mitigated: `DELETE /api/v1/runs/{id}` grants the same power by design (run_handlers.go:918-928) — parity defect, not privilege escalation.

## F6 · LOW — identifier sanitization gaps reach raw terminal sinks; Windows path redaction literal can never match

`Target.Validate` and `safeEventValue` reject only NUL/CR/LF (`runcontrol/model.go:186`, `sanitize.go:108`) — ESC passes; web transport never charset-validates `options.stage/task/shard` (`mapOperationRequest` validates scope only). Persisted Stage/Task render unescaped via `fmt.Fprintf` in `renderRunSnapshot` (`run_commands.go:416-435`) and `run follow` (`:172`), enabling ANSI escape injection from durable values into operator terminals (local-process attacker today; governed-file-derived task ids are the realistic remote-content vector). Also `safeProjectedText` redacts `` `C:\\Users\\` `` (double backslashes, `web/operations.go:647`) which matches no real Windows path.

# Defended / non-issues (checked, not reported)

- **Empty-session cancel-any** (`operations.go:350`): reachable only from `drainAndWait`; middleware guarantees non-empty signed sessions for all HTTP requests (`security.go:110-119`).
- **Web replay protection vs API-IDEMP-001**: single-use token bound to (session, canonical, fingerprint) plus durable alias surviving compaction (FK cascade only on run deletion, sqlite.go:306-314, `_foreign_keys=on`) — sound within retention horizon.
- **Cancellation reason spelling divergence** (`user_request`/`user_requested`/"QA cancellation requested"/CLI canonical set): `RequestCancellation` treats reasons as opaque validated strings (`lifecycle.go:77-80`); no consumer branches on values — cosmetic audit-text inconsistency only.
- **Raw `tool_arguments/result/error` in live SSE** (`operations.go:265`): browser shares the workspace trust domain; durable store applies allowlist + secret screening (`runcontrol/sanitize.go:10-104`), live view intentionally richer, bounded by 16 KiB substitution.
- **Cross-door alias collision**: three disjoint keyspaces (session+token hash, canonical+fingerprint hash, absent) cannot mis-dedup each other; quota-conflict misread as alias-conflict resolves NotFound safely (`durable_operations.go:106-111`).
- **`hub.start(session, prepared)`** is test-only; production uses `startConfirmed`.
- Baseline: `tui`, `web`, `runcontrol` suites pass at `5d54525`. Out-of-scope observation for the study-runloop reviewer: `TestStudyRunLoopCommandHelpInvalidFlagsAndSuccess` hangs inside `study.Service.RunLoop` select (run_loop.go:394) in a clean worktree — pre-existing, blocks the full `internal/app` suite.
